item.title: perf(ci): cache the Node toolchain instead of refetching it every job
item.summary: perf(ci): cache the Node toolchain instead of refetching it every job Blacksmith's image tracks an older runner-images snapshot. Measured on a leased box 2026-08-16, its toolcache holds Node 20.20.0, 22.22.0 and 24.13.0 while this repo's engines floor is >=22.22.3 and >=24.15.0 -- short by three and two patches. Every candidate is rejected, so all 306 of 306 sampled jobs fell through to a nodejs.org download. GitHub-hosted runners carry 24.19.0 and resolve from the toolcache in about a second, which is why only Blacksmith pays. Normally that download is 2.6s (p99 3.3s), but ~46 jobs fetch the same 50 MB simultaneously and the mirror throttles: three of 53 sampled runs had setup-node medians of 44-93s with maxes to 139s, and because every job pays at once it lands whole on the wall -- those runs went ~210s to 325s. Keep the payload in the Actions cache, which Blacksmith serves from its colocated backend. Measured on Blacksmith: cold 1605ms, warm 77ms. Restores are prefix-keyed and the save carries the resolved patch.
